prospect.name: Peter Tseng
prospect.location: West Los Angeles, California, USA (Pacific time) — names Santa Monica, Venice, Culver City and Marina del Rey as his area
prospect.occupation: Founder and operator of a mindfulness business called Open, started in 2018, offering breathwork, meditation, yoga and some Pilates. Still running it but past the 180-hour-week phase — in the office three days a week and working from home two.
prospect.family_status: Married. Wife not currently pregnant; planning a first child and describes the next year as the window before it gets harder.
prospect.training_background: Was in excellent shape through 2018 at roughly 160 lb and about 10% body fat, training with his sister's strength coach — a coach who also worked with Naomi Osaka — doing explosive plyometrics, running and sprinting, plus basketball. Founded a company and lost the physical base. Currently runs four unstructured strands weekly: a traditional strength personal trainer with supported-back work, solo bodyweight training (pull-ups, push-ups, dips), his physical therapy stack, and classes including yoga, Pilates and a 'primal moves' functional movement class. Owns substantial home equipment — a portable pull-up rack, dip station, bench press and kettlebells. Takes creatine. Describes himself as knowledgeable about nutrition and physiology.
prospect.medical: SEVERE AND ACTIVE. Herniated a disc at L5-S1 squatting, then sustained repeated re-injuries returning to athletic activity. Developed radicular symptoms — could not carry luggage upstairs and his foot went numb from nerve involvement. While in physical therapy, performing a weighted sled pull, he RUPTURED the disc with intense shooting pain. Spent roughly three months with 80% of his time horizontal. Elected conservative management over surgery and has since used a combination of chiropractor, bodywork and a DRX spinal decompression machine. AT THE TIME OF THIS CALL HE IS WEARING A BACK BRACE following a fresh setback days earlier doing kettlebell swings with 22 pounds. He states his own restrictions unprompted: must avoid axial load, deadlifts, spinal flexion, and says he will stay away from kettlebell swings for now. Currently can only bend by using a goblet-squat pattern with a vertical spine. Separately: mildly lactose intolerant. Reports he injures himself most when he has not slept well.

signals: Not recovering from a bad season — in the middle of one. He is in a back brace on the call and re-injured himself days earlier on the exact modality being sold
Motivation is extremely high and price resistance is zero — he closed at full price in under an hour and asked nothing about cost until minute forty
Training is explicitly part of fighting the condition: 'I need to do it in a way that builds muscle around the injury'
Fits the profile's operational warning exactly — easy to close, and the single most important prospect in this batch to screen clinically

STRONG ALTERNATE, near-equal weight — the_rebuilder. His own framing is pure rebuild: 'I want to get back to 2018', 160 lb and 10% body fat versus 190 lb and 20% now, and he speaks about missing the plyometric training with visible regret

Also arguable — the_medically_constrained. High intent, no price resistance, and an injury the programme may genuinely not be able to work around given that swings, deadlifts, axial load and spinal flexion are all excluded. It differs only in that no clinician had blocked him; nobody asked one
Held at 0.60 because three profiles have real claims and the choice matters less than the clinical fact underneath all of them

goals.text: Get back to his 2018 condition — 190 to 200 lb at roughly 10% body fat while keeping the muscle
Realise his physical potential, which he describes as a long-held dream
Be physically ready before the first baby arrives, because he expects it to get much harder afterwards
Be able to bend over and pick up a 10-pound baby or a 20-pound toddler without a back flare-up
Build muscle around the injury so the back stops being the thing that stops him
Have a structured three-month progression instead of four ad hoc strands that feel random
Train at high intensity again the way he did with the plyometrics coach, without aggravating the disc
Be pushed harder than his current personal trainer pushes him

pains.text: Ruptured L5-S1 disc with a history of nerve involvement and foot numbness, three months largely horizontal, currently in a back brace after a fresh flare-up from kettlebell swings at 22 lb
Cannot perform spinal flexion, axial load, deadlifts or kettlebell swings — a restriction list that removes most of the modality he is buying
Fear of another setback is the explicit condition of purchase — 'it's mostly just having an intelligent programming so that I don't have a setback'
Four separate training strands with no coordination between them — 'I'm just kind of like working out' and 'it feels random'
No progression plan — 'I don't have like a sense of like, okay, the next three months, here's the progression that I'm trying to build'
Existing personal trainer is not pushing him hard enough and will not get him to his goal
Lost his physical base entirely between 2018 and now while building the company — 160 lb at 10% body fat down to 190 lb at 20%
Nutrition execution is inconsistent — 'my ceiling is actually pretty good' but discipline collapses socially and when groceries run out
Time pressure from the planned first child — believes the window closes once the baby arrives
Only enjoys about half the healthy food he prepares

objections.raw_quote: my main questions were just like, given that I have this set of injuries, you know, is this the right, uh, program for me? So that was kind of a curiosity if, if, you know, we could work around the injuries.
objections.rep_response: Deferred it for twenty minutes, then answered with an assertion rather than a clinical consideration: 'Look, I'm very confident that Trevor can help you.' No question was asked about the brace, the rupture, the current flare-up or whether any of his four clinicians had cleared loaded kettlebell work.

objections.raw_quote: That's the only thing that would be like, oh, is this potentially not a fit? And if it's like, oh, you know, we don't think that this type of workout actually is good for someone with a back injury, you know, you should go over here instead.
objections.rep_response: 'Yeah. Yeah, absolutely. I understand. Look, I'm very confident that Trevor can help you.' The prospect had just handed the rep an explicit invitation to disqualify him and it was declined without examination.

objections.raw_quote: Do you know if Trevor's worked with anyone with a back injury?
objections.rep_response: Answered with a volume claim rather than a case or a method: 'I would say back injury, back pain, or something around back and hips is the most common thing that people are coming in with.' Then routed the clinical detail to the post-payment onboarding call: 'during the onboarding session, just let them know what exactly went through with your condition.'

objections.raw_quote: I kind of am feeling like, oh, maybe I should wait two weeks so that my back can heal up from this recent flare-up.
objections.rep_response: Offered a week, then immediately pulled the timeline forward instead — 'Or even you can meet with Trevor earlier, and he will give you something to work with before, like, even some movements' — and booked the onboarding call for the following afternoon.

objections.raw_quote: And is it okay for me to meet Trevor first before finalizing the payment? Or do I need to finalize the payment before?
objections.rep_response: 'Yeah. That's... That's the process that we have.' The prospect accepted it and paid. Proposed label: request_to_validate_fit_before_paying.

evidence: Payment taken and confirmed on the call — 'Okay. So we, we got the payment. Now let's, let's get you with Trevor.'
Paid in full at $6,000 for six months; the prospect volunteered 'We're going to dive right in and commit' and 'I'll just take care of this now'.
Agreement signed live — 'I see you already signed the agreement' — which is the only call in this batch where the on-call signature step actually ran.
Onboarding call with Trevor booked for 3:15pm the following day, and the welcome email, Skool community and onboarding form were all confirmed.

Counter-evidence on the quality of the decision, not the fact of it: the prospect asked three separate times whether the programme was clinically appropriate for a ruptured disc and never received an answer, and asked to meet the coach before paying and was told the process does not allow it.
Counter-evidence: he proposed delaying two weeks for his back to heal and the rep moved the start earlier rather than later.
outcome.next_step: Onboarding call with Trevor at 3:15pm the following day. Prospect to complete the onboarding form and log into the Primal University Skool community beforehand, and to describe his back condition to Trevor on that call. The rep also gave the prospect his personal WhatsApp number and asked to stay in touch about his progress.

notable.note: The most serious call in this batch. A 34-year-old with a ruptured L5-S1 disc, a documented history of nerve involvement and foot numbness, three months spent largely horizontal, currently wearing a back brace after re-injuring himself on a 22 lb kettlebell swing days earlier, asked three times whether this programme was appropriate for him, offered the rep an explicit opening to disqualify him, asked to speak to the coach before paying, and proposed waiting two weeks for his back to settle. He was reassured, told the process requires payment first, moved to an earlier start, and paid $6,000. Not one question was asked about his chiropractor, his physical therapist, the DRX decompression treatment or whether any of them had cleared loaded ballistic training. Separately, when he asked directly how the payment broke down, the instalment options the same rep offered another prospect the previous day were not disclosed. On process the call is otherwise strong — P11 ran to the letter, including the on-call signature.

quality.notes: Sustained inversion, worst in the opening ten minutes where the prospect's injury history alternates between labels mid-sentence — 'I was pulling, I was doing a weighted, that's what it's called, a sled pull' is attributed to the rep but is plainly the prospect continuing his own account. Several of the rep's discovery questions carry the prospect's label and vice versa throughout. The body-composition figures come through mangled as '$1.60' and '$1.90' and are read as 160 lb and 190 lb from context. The injury year reads as '2004' which is inconsistent with the 2018 company founding and the surrounding narrative; recorded as an apparent transcription error and not relied upon. Roles read from content throughout.
